definition: Co-training is a machine learning algorithm used when there are only small amounts of labeled data and large amounts of unlabeled data.
details: One of its uses is in text mining for search engines. It was introduced by Avrim Blum and Tom Mitchell in 1998.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. In plain words: Co-training is a machine learning algorithm used when there are only small amounts of labeled data and large amounts of unlabeled data. Here is how it actually plays out: One of its uses is in text mining for search engines. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Co-training.
